A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Open-YOLO 3D, with matching main sections, equations and benchmark tables. All supplied material is readable. v1 ends with references; v3 adds Appendix A with Figures 5–20.

before.justification: Tables 1–5 report original ScanNet200 and Replica experiments, including segmentation accuracy, inference times and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds runtime breakdowns and qualitative prediction and confidence-ranking analyses in its appendix.

M1.justification: The Mask3D proposals, YOLO-World label maps, accelerated visibility computation, MVPDist and combined mask/class confidence score are unchanged. Appendix Figures 5–6 illustrate existing procedures without establishing an algorithm modification.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation on ScanNet200 and Replica using generated and ground-truth masks. The appendix adds examples within these datasets and the existing text-prompting task, without introducing a distinct domain or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 and the retained qualitative comparisons is unchanged. The additional runtime and qualitative figures use already-evaluated OpenMask3D and Open3DIS, without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: The original splits, AP metrics, frame sampling and model configurations remain unchanged. Added diagnostics report timing by pipeline stage in Figure 7 and explicitly inspect highest-scoring and top-two predictions in Figures 9–11, extending the evaluation procedures in a limited way.

E4.justification: The detector, MVPDist, visibility, view-count and label-granularity ablations in Tables 3–4 are retained. Figures 7–11 add focused runtime diagnostics, an HG/LG distribution comparison and confidence-ranking case studies, including an example of a mask extending into another instance.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests for benchmark performance. Means and standard deviations of prompt-ID distributions already appear in v1 Figure 3; their additional display does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, including 24.7 mAP on ScanNet200 and 23.7 on Replica. v3 adds component timings, an HG prompt-distribution example and qualitative segmentation/ranking outputs in Figures 7–20. Changing Table 3's '675,6' to '675.6' is equivalent numerical formatting.

T1.justification: The projection and visibility equations, MVPDist definition and confidence-score formula are unchanged. Appendix diagrams and worked examples introduce no new mathematical definition, formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about detection-based labeling, proposal scoring, benchmark performance and speedup. The appendix supplies additional support without changing these claims' scope.

C2.justification: Figure 11 adds a mechanism explanation for poor confidence rankings: highly visible points can dominate aggregated CLIP features and give defective masks high semantic scores. This extends the existing discussion of mask quality versus semantic confidence; the main small-object limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 5 explicitly shows selected top-k views feeding per-view maximum-IoU calculations and subsequent averaging, expanding the scoring documentation. Figure 6 illustrates HG-map construction. The stated models, frame sampling, hardware and code/model access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 58 references are retained. The positioning of detection-based labeling relative to SAM/CLIP-based approaches and the claimed novelty remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 1–6 retain their wording and organization almost entirely. Appendix A adds explanatory captions and case descriptions, accompanied by a decimal-separator correction and updated version metadata; there is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with Figures 5–20: computational diagrams, runtime and distribution plots, confidence comparisons and segmentation galleries. Existing figures and tables are preserved, while reference-list spacing becomes tighter.

improvement.justification: The appendix provides scoring illustrations previously referenced but absent from v1, exposes runtime bottlenecks in Figure 7 and adds concrete confidence-ranking evidence in Figure 11. These improve clarity and support for the existing claims. The main quantitative evaluation is unchanged, and the added ranking evidence consists of selected qualitative cases, so the overall gain is limited.
